dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent, and I'll be evaluating the skin condition on your left hand today. To start, how long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any changes in its appearance recently?
I first noticed this patch on the back of my left hand a few months ago. It hasn't really changed much lately, but it feels very rough and scaly, almost like a piece of sandpaper.
That sounds quite uncomfortable. Does the area ever itch, bleed, or cause you any pain, and have you spent a lot of time in the sun over the years? REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination

RESULTS: Temperature: 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure: 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate: 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate: 14 breaths/min. Inspection reveals a rough, scaly plaque on the left dorsal hand. No tenderness or pain upon palpation.

It's important to know if that area has ever bled or if you have any other similar spots elsewhere on your body. Also, do you have a history of significant sun exposure or any personal or family history of skin cancer? REQUEST TEST: Dermoscopy
Since the dermoscopy was unremarkable, I’d like to know if the spot ever bleeds or forms a crust that falls off and returns? Also, have you ever worked outdoors or had any previous skin

It doesn't really bleed, but sometimes it gets a bit crusty or flaky before the rough texture returns. I’ve never worked outdoors for a living, but I do spend a lot of time outside walking and sunbathing.
Have you ever tried applying any over-the-counter creams or ointments to this spot, and if so, did they help at all? Also, do you have any history of other health

I've tried putting some moisturizer on it, but it doesn't seem to smooth out that sandpaper feel at all. As for my health, I've just been managing my diabetes and high blood pressure with my usual medications.
To help me get a better picture, what color is the patch, and roughly how large would you say it is? Also, has it grown significantly since you first noticed it? REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
RESULTS: Skin biopsy findings show hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis, consistent with actinic keratosis.

Oh, I see. Since you've confirmed what it is, does this mean the sunbathing I enjoy is what caused that rough patch to form? Is it something we can treat easily here in the office?

Yes, actinic keratosis is directly linked to chronic sun exposure, so your sunbathing history is the likely cause. It is easily treated here in the office with procedures like cryotherapy or prescription
That makes sense, and I'm relieved to hear it can be handled right here today. Will the cryotherapy leave a scar, and do I need to start wearing gloves or extra sunscreen when I go for my walks?

Cryotherapy might cause a small blister or temporary redness, but it typically heals well with very little scarring. I highly recommend using a high-SPF sunscreen and protective clothing during your walks to prevent new

Keep the treated area clean and apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly to help it heal. I recommend a follow-up skin exam every six to twelve months to monitor for any new spots.
